deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a German prose note on Hellenistic (Seleucid) history and continues the narrative of the previous and next pages. In order, it covers:

(1) The end of Seleucus II Callinicus: in 238 he tries to take Parthia, is captured, and the note says he died in captivity in 227.

(2) His son Seleucus III Ceraunus reigns 3 years, with his cousin Achaeus conducting affairs. In 223, during an expedition (apparently in Asia Minor / across the Taurus), he is poisoned because he wanted to borrow money.

(3) His brother Antiochus III Magnus succeeds at age 15 (margin '15 J. alt'). He is under the influence or guardianship of Hermias. In his first year he fights the revolts of Molon and Alexander in Media and Persis (margin 'Alexander u Molo').

(4) Achaeus revolts in Asia Minor ('Vorderasien'), after Hermias accuses him of disloyalty, and takes up arms in 220. Margin: 'bis 215 hielt er sich' (he held out until 215).

(5) Hermias is killed (dated 218 in the note).

(6) Antiochus tries to seize the Ptolemaic possessions and in 217 marches against Ptolemy IV Philopator. He is defeated at Raphia.

(7) In 215 he captures Achaeus. In 214 he starts an eastern expedition (the anabasis) that lasts 9 years.

There are no formulas, numbers or derivations beyond chronological dates. Nothing can be reconstructed mathematically. These look like lecture or study notes on ancient history, and the hand may not even be Gauss's.
errors: Historical slip: Seleucus II was not captured by the Parthians. That fate belongs to Demetrius II (c. 138 BC). Seleucus II was defeated by Arsaces around 238 and died in a fall from a horse around 225.

Historical slip: 'Unter ihm kam Syrien an Rom' is inaccurate. Under Antiochus III, Syria came into conflict with Rome (peace of Apamea, 188). Syria became a Roman province only in 64 BC, under Pompey.
Chronology: Hermias was eliminated around 220 BC (before the Fourth Syrian War), not 218. The death of Seleucus II is usually dated 225, not 227.
deep.surprise_reason: The page is purely historical prose notes on Seleucid kings, with no mathematical content. Such notes are routine and of no significance for the history of mathematics.

Line 9: 'unter der Herrschaft[?]' is uncertain. The word in the image is not clearly 'Herrschaft' and may be 'Vormundschaft' or 'Botmäßigkeit'.
Line 15: 'Hermias wurde 218 hi[?] vergiftet[?]' may read 'hingerichtet' ('hin gerichtet') rather than 'vergiftet'.
Line 16: 'sich[?] der Länder wieder[?]' is uncertain. The verb may be 'bemächtigen', with the line ending 'in Aegypten besaßen'.
